entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page_history
entries.description:
Get a historical version of a specific Confluence page.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID.
    version: The version number to retrieve.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content at the specified version.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'.

version.description: The version number of the page to retrieve

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

content.text:
All three pages retrieved. Report below.

---

## 1. Page 312377345 — TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes

### Conformity / certificate / document / PDF attribute: **does not exist**

I walked all 51 defined attributes (16 system + 4 existing custom + 31 new custom), the 7 "not in scope" rows, and the ~30 ignored-Magento-fields list. There is **no** attribute for a declaration of conformity, certificate, compliance document, PDF, file, or asset URL of any kind. The word "conformity" does not appear on the page. A site-wide Confluence search for "Declaration of Conformity" returns nothing relevant either — **this blocker is genuinely unanswered anywhere in Confluence, not just unanswered on this page.**

The only document-ish things in the whole attribute set are images (handled outside the attribute model) and video (`vidnote`, explicitly excluded and pushed to a custom object):

> | `vidnote` |  | Handled in custom object pending TSD: TSD: SFCC-799 — Product Video Gallery Management |

### The two precedent patterns that matter for your estimate

**(a) The `sizeGuide` pattern — attribute-as-key, content in Contentful.** This is the closest existing precedent to "attribute points at a document", and it argues for a fourth option your blocker doesn't list:

> | `sizeGuide` | Size guide indicator key — identifies which size guide applies to this product | `Kids` | **Enum-of-string...** | Master / Variation group | No | No | **SFCC** | `size_guide` | — | Storefront Attributes | Attribute value is a lookup key only. Actual size guide content is authored and stored in **Contentful**. The PWA resolves the Contentful entry using this key at runtime. **Requires MuleSoft business rule & remapping** |

**(b) A DAM already exists, but only for imagery.** Open item #4, status Closed:

> | 4 | Product imagery source | Zimmermann Digital | Closed | External DAM → MuleSoft → SFCC |

The DAM is named nowhere on the page and its scope is stated as imagery only. Whether it can hold a PDF and expose a stable URL is not documented.

### EU compliance precedent — note the attribute name is not what you have

You referenced `showEnvironmentalNote`. The attribute in the authoritative list is **`environmentalNotes`** — a Text field, not a boolean:

> | `environmentalNotes` | Sustainability / environmental notes | `Sustainably sourced` | Text | Master / Variation Group | No | No | **AP21** | `enviro_notes` | text | Storefront Attributes | Currently manual upload into AP21, this is front-end facing, EU/FR site relevant **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

So the precedent pattern is: **content lives in the attribute itself, sourced from AP21 via manual upload, and the accordion renders only when the field is populated.** There is no separate boolean "show" flag — presence of data is the gate. Worth correcting in the estimate, because it changes the shape of what you'd be asking for.

### Product type / sunglasses discriminator: **no clean one exists**

Four candidates, all imperfect. Verbatim:

> | `ap21Category` | Internal AP21 ERP category code | `Tops` | String | Master | No | No | **AP21** | `categoryap21` | text | Zimmermann Product Data | Hidden, not searchable — ERP reference only, not storefront nav - top level category (e.g. Tops) **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

> | `productLine` | Information from AP21 on the Product line | Swim Lycra | String | Master |  |  | AP21 | `prodline` |  | — | This information can be used by the content team to correctly map a product to a category - but this is not a category in itself. This drives the swatch-image set on PDP (apparel vs. Accessories) **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

> | `productSub` | Further information from AP21 on the Product line | Bikini Triangle | String | Master |  |  | AP21 | `prodsub` |  | — | This information can be used by the content team to correctly map a product to a category - but this is not a category in itself **Requires MuleSoft remapping** |

> | `label` | Merchandising product line | `Ready to Wear` | **Enum-of-string** | Master | No | Yes | **AP21** | `label` | select (3 options) | Zimmermann Product Data | Options: `Projects`, `Ready to Wear`, `Swim` ... |

`productLine`/`productSub` are free-text strings with no controlled value list, and both are explicitly "not a category in itself". `ap21Category` is hidden and non-searchable. `label`'s three options don't cover accessories at all.

## Bottom line for the audit

The blocker is real and **cannot be closed from existing documentation** — no storage mechanism, no attribute, no requirement, and no precedent for a per-product binary asset exists anywhere across the three authoritative pages. The estimate cannot be de-risked by a doc read; it needs a decision. Three things I'd add to the ticket before estimating:

1. The `sizeGuide` → Contentful pattern is a fourth option your blocker doesn't list, and is the only *proven* per-product-document-ish mechanism in the codebase's world. A DoC is a signed static PDF per style, which is closer to a Contentful asset than to a BM attribute value.
2. The discriminator question has no good answer today. No attribute identifies sunglasses; the category tree can, but exposes three nodes, no documented IDs, and is merchandiser-mutable and marked In progress.
3. Storefront scope diverges from the precedent: PRD-009 covers `EN-EU, FR-EU` only. "EU and EU International" is a wider scope than any confirmed EU-compliance requirement currently has.
